about: Feature ledger of the upstream parity tracker (apaki/parity/PARITY.md). One entry per feature Apaki supports or plans. Edit by hand; npm test checks the shape.

features.title: Run the real Claude Code per pane through the Agent SDK
features.notes: One SessionRunner (its own Claude Code process, model, effort, mode, billing) per pane, Claude Code preset system prompt, user, project and local setting sources, so CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP and slash commands work as in the terminal. latch (terminal) shares src/runner.js.

features.title: Replies stream and render like Claude Code: markdown, tool lines with results, red and green diffs
features.notes: Nested and task lists, tables, quotes, highlighted code. Tool inputs are read from the tool_use blocks, so a new field on a tool input is a change to watch for here.

features.title: Working line uses Claude Code spinner words (Cogitating, Noodling, Percolating)
features.notes: A copy of Claude Code's 179 spinner verbs (verbs.js); a random one per turn and per new stretch of thinking. Re-check the list when Claude Code changes its spinner set.

features.title: Model, effort and permission mode pickers per conversation
features.notes: Chips under the message box; Shift+Tab cycles the mode; effort is a dot grid. Not exposed: permission modes auto and dontAsk (permission-mode ids exist upstream). Phone ops model, effort and mode are in PHONE_OPS, clamped by the phone capability.

features.title: Permission modes auto and dontAsk
features.notes: The SDK has six permission modes; Apaki offers four (bypassPermissions, acceptEdits, plan, default). Not requested by Arthur; recorded because the id exists upstream.

features.title: Allow or deny card in the pane when Claude Code asks to use a tool
features.notes: 2026-10-12: built. engine.js passes every pane the callback from permissions.js, which holds the call, sends an ask event with a permission block (the SDK's title, displayName, description, decisionReason, blockedPath, defaultToNo and the suggestions as words) and settles it from the window's or phone's answer op: Allow once, Always allow (the SDK's suggestions returned as updatedPermissions, never rules from the client; suppressAlwaysAllowRule is respected) or Deny with a note (the note is Claude's message). Enter allows once (not in the first 600 ms, not when defaultToNo) and Esc denies. Answered once; the sheet drops (ask_gone) when the signal aborts, the main turn ends or the process ends; a subagent's prompt survives a main result. A phone's blocked tools are refused first (capCanUseTool); only a Full phone may save a rule. Apaki's own show tool (mcp__apaki__show, from the in-process server) is allowed without a prompt; its browser tools are asked about like any MCP tool. Before this, anything that would prompt was auto-allowed (observed 2026-10-11). Not covered: the permission_denied message still shows as a Permission line, not a sheet; AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode keep their own sheets. 2026-10-12, later (Arthur: "it should be shown in the pane and not lock the user from using the app"): no longer a sheet over the window. It is a card in the pane that asked, docked above its message box (apaki/ui/askcard.js), numbered rows like Claude Code's terminal; the rest of the window stays usable, several panes can wait at once, numbers and Enter answer only the focused pane's card, Esc goes back to the message box without answering, the tab and the header say Waiting for you and the taskbar badge counts it; ask_gone carries why and by, so a card settled elsewhere leaves one line (Answered on a phone, the turn ended).

features.title: AskUserQuestion card in the pane, answered once, waits up to 7 days
features.notes: In bypassPermissions the SDK never calls canUseTool, so AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode are answered from a programmatic PreToolUse hook (matcher AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode). The hook timeout is ASK_TIMEOUT_S = 7 days (src/runner.js) so a slow answer is never dropped and asked again. The engine settles questions nobody waits for and the window drops the stale sheet (ask_gone). Sheet supports multiple questions, multi-select and a typed answer. 2026-10-12, later (Arthur: "it should be shown in the pane and not lock the user from using the app"): no longer a sheet over the window. It is a card in the pane that asked, docked above its message box (apaki/ui/askcard.js), numbered rows like Claude Code's terminal; the rest of the window stays usable, several panes can wait at once, numbers and Enter answer only the focused pane's card, Esc goes back to the message box without answering, the tab and the header say Waiting for you and the taskbar badge counts it; ask_gone carries why and by, so a card settled elsewhere leaves one line (Answered on a phone, the turn ended).

features.title: Plan approval card in the pane (Ready to code?)
features.notes: Approve switches the pane out of plan mode; Keep planning denies. A chat-only phone cannot carry out a plan: the engine answers ExitPlanMode before asking that phone (engine.js). 2026-10-12, later (Arthur: "it should be shown in the pane and not lock the user from using the app"): no longer a sheet over the window. It is a card in the pane that asked, docked above its message box (apaki/ui/askcard.js), numbered rows like Claude Code's terminal; the rest of the window stays usable, several panes can wait at once, numbers and Enter answer only the focused pane's card, Esc goes back to the message box without answering, the tab and the header say Waiting for you and the taskbar badge counts it; ask_gone carries why and by, so a card settled elsewhere leaves one line (Answered on a phone, the turn ended).

features.title: Steer: add a message to the running turn (Ctrl+Enter)
features.notes: A user message pushed into the live input stream without a priority is folded in at Claude's next step; the turn ends with one result (measured 2026-10-09). Never priority now (it interrupts). Works in any running turn, including ones Claude started itself. Phones can steer since 1a55d53.

features.title: Queue messages while Claude works; Edit; engine sends them with the window closed
features.notes: Enter with a draft while Claude works queues it in a tray (Steer, remove, click or Up to edit). The pane sends its queue to the engine (op queueSet) so a closed window does not strand it. Phone: the queue stays in the phone pane and the engine never sends one for a phone (remote-policy.js comment), so a phone that closes the page loses the benefit.

features.title: Stop a running turn (Esc, Stop button)
features.notes: Enter on an empty box does nothing; only Esc or Stop interrupts.

features.title: Slash commands from Claude Code's own list, plus Apaki's /resume, /warm, /key
features.notes: The / menu lists supportedCommands (about 140 on the build machine) and sends them through; interactive-only built-ins are handled or declined with a reason. /resume and /continue open the sidebar session search (d0b106d). Not yet used: terminal_slash_commands on the init message (hide terminal-bound commands on the phone), and the commands_changed message (list refresh).

features.title: Context meter chip with bar, breakdown and Compact now
features.notes: getContextUsage in summary mode (the numbers behind /context, no extra API calls), measured after the process starts, after every turn and after a compaction. Before a conversation runs, context-estimate.js reads the last reply's usage from the transcript tail and shows an estimate. Phones use the contextUsage op.

features.title: Auto-compact off by default; Settings choice (Off, 200k, 300k, 500k, default)
features.notes: A new install passes { autoCompactEnabled: false, idleCompaction: false } per process through the SDK settings option, never a settings file. Verified live against the bundled Claude Code: getContextUsage reported isAutoCompactEnabled false with it. The size choices pass { autoCompactWindow: n } the same way (prefs.js compactSettings); default passes nothing. Compact now and /compact summarize by hand. The phone never sets it (PC setting, remote-policy.js).

features.title: Show compaction in the conversation and say when it fails
features.notes: Status compacting shows on the working line; compact_boundary prints "Conversation compacted."; a failed compaction (status compact_result failed) is an error line. History keeps compaction markers.

features.title: Show what Claude Code shows: blocked prompts, hook output, retries, limits, denials
features.notes: Arthur 2026-10-11: show ALL output a Claude Code user sees, including the yellow text when a prompt is caught, in a visibly different style. noticeFor maps each SDK message to a system line (monospace, label Hook, API, Limit, Permission, Model or Recap, yellow, gray or red, no capsule or stripe). The runner asks for hook events and drops the quiet ones (quietHookEvent) before they reach a window or phone. The yellow text is a system informational at level warning, also how the prompt relay answers arrive. History shows the same lines (systemNote, hookNote). The HOOK_WORDS list in notices.js names 11 of the 33 hook events; a new event with a hook-shaped informational line would need adding there.

features.title: Usage limit warnings and rejections, once each, with the reset time
features.notes: allowed_warning and rejected statuses become Limit lines with the percentage and reset time; repeated warnings are suppressed through the pane's seen map. Auto-continue after reset is a separate planned feature.

features.title: Tasks button: subagents, shells and monitors you can see, open, drag and stop
features.notes: Live task list per conversation with type, model, time, tokens, current tool and Claude's one-line summary; open one in a viewer that follows it live (a subagent's own conversation, a shell's output) as a split or tab; stop one or send it to the background. Sessions in the list show their subagent count, including terminal sessions. Phone: the task chips arrive in the shared pane, but the viewer ops (agentWatch, outputWatch, taskStop, taskBackground) are not in PHONE_OPS.

features.title: Attach and paste images into a message
features.notes: png, jpeg, gif and webp only for a phone (IMAGE_TYPES). The SDK image limit (2000 px per axis for the API) is the engine's concern: see the global image size safety rule before reading images into context.

features.title: Rewind: restore files and conversation to an earlier turn
features.notes: Half built: enableFileCheckpointing is already on so /rewind works back in the terminal on a session edited in Apaki (runner.js); there is no rewind UI. Market research 2026-10-11 ranks it P0 (Codex #9203 /undo 477 thumbs-up, #11626 /rewind 227). Not yet approved by Arthur as a build item.

features.title: Claude Code prompt suggestions (a predicted next prompt after each turn)
features.notes: Not built and not requested; recorded so the upstream ids are reviewed rather than unreviewed.

features.title: Every session on the machine, live, including headless and terminal ones
features.notes: Arthur 2026-10-09: "we CANNOT miss anything. we must see all sessions, and it should be live". The SDK list drops sessions whose first entry is headless (2 of 224 here were real conversations), so the engine merges its own scan of the transcripts. Sessions open in terminals come from ~/.claude/sessions live records (not in the SDK) and refresh about every 2 s.

features.title: Open in terminal view and auto-import of sessions open in terminal windows
features.notes: Reads Claude Code's live records (~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json, entrypoint cli, live pid), not an SDK surface, so an upstream change to that record format shows up only as a broken list. Watch for it on every Claude Code upgrade.

features.title: Full conversation history read from the transcript, paged
features.notes: getSessionMessages returns only the chain after the last compaction (a 2925 message session showed 400); history.js reads the JSONL itself, keeps compaction markers, hook and system notes, and pages with historyBefore and historyBlock (phones too). Depends on the transcript line format, which is not versioned: re-run the history tests after every Claude Code upgrade.

features.title: Session list times from the last real message
features.notes: Claude Code writes bookkeeping lines (cost-state, last-prompt, turn_duration, recaps) on open, resume and close, so the file modified time lied (12 of the 60 newest looked fresh, really 13 to 90 hours old). Reads each transcript tail for the last real message. Depends on the transcript line types.

features.title: Rename a session by double-clicking its title; saved in the session like /rename
features.notes: One name, saved with the SDK renameSession so Claude Code, latch and Apaki agree. Phone (2026-10-12): Rename is in the session menu (long press on a list row, or the ... button of a conversation) and asks in a sheet; the rename op is a phone op for Full and No shell access and is refused for Chat only (remote-policy.js capAllowsOp). The page shows it only for a PC whose hello lists the op.

features.title: Session context menu: stop, fork, archive, reveal folder, open in new tab
features.notes: Arthur 2026-10-10: "think of what codex and claude desktop would let you do". A click opens a session in a new tab; right click offers the menu. Phone (2026-10-12): the same menu as a sheet from the bottom, opened by a long press on a list row (native.js makes the contextmenu event iOS never sends) or the ... button in the conversation bar: Find, Open, Open in a new pane of the current tab, Stop (this phone's own turn), Close, Rename, Fork, Archive, Copy session id, Copy resume command, Move to folder. forkSession and archive are phone ops for Full and No shell; Chat only sees them dimmed with the reason. Left out on purpose, so the phone stays partial: Show folder (it opens Explorer on the PC) and Stop for a turn that runs in another window (stopSession acts on panes the phone does not own).

features.title: Session folders: create, rename, drag sessions in and out
features.notes: Folders live in ~/.claude/latch/folders.json (Apaki's own, not Claude Code's). Phone: the folders list arrives as a broadcast (BROADCAST_EVENTS) so a phone shows the grouping. Since 2026-10-12 the session menu moves a session into a folder, takes it out, and makes a folder (New folder asks in a sheet): the folder op takes only the actions move and create, for Full and No shell access. Still on the PC, so the phone stays partial: renaming and deleting folders, and dragging.

features.title: Deep system-wide session search by words and by meaning
features.notes: latch-index is a Rust (tantivy) full text index over every Claude Code transcript (8,739 files, 18.7 GB on the build PC), plus a local embedding model for meaning. Phones use the search op and the index and meaning broadcasts (checked on the phone page in the demo harness 2026-10-12: results by words and by meaning, with the by-meaning mark). The index reads transcripts directly, so it follows transcript format changes, not SDK changes.

features.title: Ask Claude and Dig deeper: model-assisted session search
features.notes: Spends the selected subscription or API credit to find sessions like "the forge.myrlin.io marketing and growth sessions". Phone (2026-10-12): Ask Claude is a button under the search box for a PC whose hello lists askSearch (body.can-ask), open to every access level because it is a Haiku call with no tools over the PC's own indexes (about a cent, billed to the phone's focused pane or the live account, like a message from it) and one question at a time per phone (AskGate). Dig deeper stays on the PC (it opens an Opus session that needs the shell tools), so the phone is partial. Decision for Arthur: the earlier note wanted the PC owner's consent per phone for Ask Claude; this treats the phone's pairing and access level as that consent.

features.title: Sessions keep running when the window closes (background engine host)
features.notes: Arthur: "apaki closing should not close the claude sessions that are open". The engine runs as a per-user host on 127.0.0.1 with an HMAC handshake; closing the window only disconnects; idle processes close after 5 minutes. This is what lets phone access survive a closed window.

features.title: Workspace saved continuously and restored after a crash
features.notes: Tabs, splits and sizes, each pane's session and settings, drafts, queued messages, scroll, open viewers, window place. Kept twice (app storage and a file on disk); the newer wins. The market research cites seven first-party reports of lost Code-tab history as the reason this matters.

features.title: Tabs and drag-to-split panes, up to six conversations per tab
features.notes: Resizable splits, drag a pane by its grip, drag tabs to reorder (12eb702), a new conversation opens as a new pane in the current tab (2010439), a click on a session opens a new tab unless the focused pane is empty (3410214). Tab and pane counts count conversations only; viewers and browsers come on top up to 10 panes. Phone: up to 6 panes (MAX_PHONE_PANES) and the desktop's tabs are shown (desktopTabs) but not arranged. 2026-10-12 (bb30acd): a tab opened in the background or restored with the window opened scrolled to the top of its conversation, because a background tab is display: none and a hidden pane has no scroll position; the pane now remembers the reader's place and applies it when it gets a box (pane.js settleScroll, test/apaki-pane-scroll.test.js), on the desktop and the phone, and the saved workspace keeps that place.

features.title: Phones see the desktop's tabs and the panes in each
features.notes: Per tab: panes in layout order, kind, title, session id, working, focus. Drafts, queues, folders and browser addresses stay on the PC.

features.title: Follow a conversation open on the desktop from the phone, without taking it over
features.notes: Tapping a desktop pane on the phone sends op follow: the phone pane shows that conversation live (messages, tool lines, thinking, questions) while the desktop keeps the pane and its one Claude Code. Take over is an action in the pane (a confirm sheet, then unfollow and a forced open), and the PC pane then says it moved. Desktop: a quiet Also on <phone> line in the pane header, and a Sent from <phone> tag on a message typed there; no pill, no dot. Access: Full may send, steer, stop and answer from the followed pane; No shell and Chat only watch (View only line, questions answered on the PC); the model, effort and mode of a followed pane are the desktop's for every level. A followed Claude or Codex pane both work. A phone that reconnects or reloads follows again instead of reopening. Looked at in the demo harness (phone.html?ws=follow-phone&follow=1, cap=chat for a restricted phone), light and dark at 390 by 844.

features.title: Ding when a session comes back or needs an answer
features.notes: Synthesized: rising when a turn finishes, falling when a session waits for an answer; toggle in Settings. Replaced in importance by the OS notification item below.

features.title: Count of ready tabs in the tab bar and the dock or taskbar badge
features.notes: Number of tabs whose conversation finished or asks while you were not looking. macOS dock badge; Windows has no number badge so an overlay icon is drawn.

features.title: OS toast and phone push when a session finishes or needs approval
features.notes: Market research P0: only the ding and the badge exist. Phone push needs a design that keeps the relay blind to content (mobile README has one); CLOUD.md lists push as a later paid item. Claude Code itself has settings for mobile push (inputNeededNotifEnabled, agentPushNotifEnabled) which would be the free route if Anthropic's own push path is usable. Not yet approved by Arthur as a build item.

features.title: Run in the tray so phone access survives closing the window
features.notes: The engine host already outlives the window (sessions-outlive-the-window); a tray icon and start-with-Windows are what is missing. Market research P1: "Unknown; check". Not yet approved by Arthur.

features.title: Auto-continue a session after a usage limit resets
features.notes: Claude Code has the setting autoContinueAtUsageLimit; the queue and Glass (which knows reset times) make this a natural fit. Claude #13354 (209 thumbs-up), #35744 (103), Codex #21073 (73). Market research P1. Not yet approved by Arthur.

features.title: Keyboard shortcut cheat sheet and command palette
features.notes: Shortcuts exist (Ctrl+B, T, W, F, F3, Ctrl+Enter, Shift+Tab) but are not listed anywhere in the app. Market research P1.

features.title: Side chat that reads the main thread (Ctrl+;)
features.notes: Market research P2. Claude Desktop has it; no Agent SDK control request for it was found in claude-sdk 0.3.295 (control_request_progress mentions side_question, which may be the hook: check before building).

features.title: Integrated terminal and file editor panes
features.notes: Market research P2. A browser pane and a viewer pane exist (artifacts, built-in browser); a terminal and an editor do not. Codex checklist asks for terminal output in the side panel.

features.title: Scheduled tasks and automations
features.notes: Market research P2; Codex automations are called its most distinctive capability. Claude Code ships Cron and ScheduleWakeup tools, so some of this is already reachable from a conversation.

features.title: Sessions on SSH hosts and in WSL
features.notes: Market research P2.

features.title: Multi-window and detachable panes
features.notes: Market research P2: Claude Desktop issues #30154 (245) and #27725 (68) ask for it; first-party apps do not have it yet.

features.title: Artifacts: Claude shows pages, documents, SVG, images and PDFs in a viewer beside the conversation
features.notes: An in-process MCP server "apaki" with the tool show (mcp__apaki__show) and one appended system prompt paragraph, passed per pane through SDK options only (nothing written to the user's settings). Every revision is kept; HTML runs sandboxed with no network. A closed viewer is remembered by its conversation and reopened from an icon beside the grip (dd070bf). Claude Code has its own Artifact tool (tool-input:Artifact in sdk-tools.d.ts); Apaki does not use it.

features.title: Catch "open this" commands and BROWSER and show them in Apaki
features.notes: A PreToolUse hook on Bash and PowerShell denies a command whose purpose is to open a URL or file in the OS ("Opened in Apaki instead") and shows it in Apaki; BROWSER points at a shim so tools that open a browser (vite --open, Python webbrowser) land in Apaki. Runs on the PC for every pane; a phone sees the result as an artifact.

features.title: Built-in browser pane that Claude can drive (open, read, click, type, back, screenshot)
features.notes: A WebView2 child webview per browser pane; pages read as an outline with numbered links, buttons and fields; pages have no access to the app or sessions. Phone: the six browser tools are blocked for No shell and Chat only phones (APAKI_BROWSER_TOOLS). 2026-10-12: a live WebView2 cannot run on a phone, so the phone gets a read-only view of the page a Full phone's own conversation opened: a Browser button in the conversation bar once Claude has used the browser there (pane.js markBrowser), opening a sheet with the page's title and address, one JPEG of the part in view (engine op browserView, browser-tools.js view, quiet so the desktop strip says nothing), what Claude just did, and Refresh; it refreshes itself a moment after each browserActivity line, so it follows Claude through the page. A web page card's Open opens a public address in the phone's own browser and a PC-only one (localhost) as this view. Left out, so the phone stays partial: clicking or typing in the PC's browser from the phone, and seeing a browser pane that a desktop conversation opened (it belongs to another window; the desktop's own pane list shows it as a quiet Browser row).

features.title: Ctrl+F finds text in the focused pane
features.notes: Frosted bar top right: every match marked, Enter and F3 step, Aa matches case, a collapsed tool block holding the match opens. Phone (2026-10-12): Find in conversation is the first item of the conversation menu (the ... button); the same bar runs full width under the conversation bar with 44 px targets, the keyboard's Search key steps, no case toggle, Previous and Next keep the keyboard, and Done does not give it to the message box.

features.title: Voice dictation with a local Whisper model
features.notes: The mic button records 16 kHz mono in the window, the engine runs whisper.cpp (b5454 CPU build) with ggml-base.en. Phones never use it (remote-policy.js: never voice); the phone keyboard has its own dictation. Marked n/a on the phone as a decision to confirm with Arthur: equal functionality would be sending phone audio to the PC.

features.title: Myrlin Glass in the corner: live accounts, switching, billing follows Glass
features.notes: The corner card shows the live Claude account (an API key reads as one, with dollars left) and the live Codex account; Glass swaps restart a Glass-following pane's runner on its next message, resumed from disk. The manage panel renames, reconnects, adds, hides and removes credentials (9cc905e). Phone: glass state is broadcast (read only); swaps and the panel are PC only (never billing ops).

features.title: Choose subscription or API key per conversation
features.notes: Any existing Claude Code conversation can continue on a Console API key in the same session file so nothing forks. Terms: Anthropic documents multiple accounts through CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; keep the market research section 5 terms notes in mind before anything hosted touches credentials.

features.title: Keep the prompt cache warm for idle API-key sessions
features.notes: A detached keeper resumes the session with the same options and persistSession false about every 52 minutes, with a daily cap. Measured on Opus 5.5: a kept-warm turn cost $0.125, the same turn left cold $0.478. Depends on cache TTL behavior, which Anthropic can change: re-measure when the SDK changes its defaults.

features.title: Corner card shows the live Codex account
features.notes: Display only, through the glass CLI. Codex panes (and account/updated, account/rateLimits/updated) are planned in codex-glass-accounts-and-limits.

features.title: Claude Code skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers and CLAUDE.md load as in the terminal
features.notes: Every pane loads user, project and local settings, so extensions work. Partial because there is no panel to see MCP server status, reconnect a server, or reload plugins and skills (the SDK has query methods for all three; latch has /mcp, Apaki does not), and plugin install messages are not shown.

features.title: Show Claude Code's todo list as a live checklist
features.notes: 2026-10-12: TodoWrite is a checklist (todos.js): pending, in progress (bold, tinted row, the present-tense form under it) and completed (struck through), one card per turn that later TodoWrite calls update in place (a new turn, or a new plan once the old one is all done, starts a new card), drawn the same live, from history (tool_use blocks) and in a subagent's viewer, on the desktop and the phone page. Still partial: the newer TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, TaskList and TaskGet tools are not rendered specially. Codex plans are planned as a checklist (codex-plans-checklist), so the Claude side should match.

features.title: Choose where a new conversation starts (Starts in sheet)
features.notes: Lists known places and lets you browse and make folders (ops places, listDir, mkdir). Phone: a phone opens a conversation but those ops are not in PHONE_OPS, so it cannot browse or choose a folder. The worktree plan adds New worktree to this sheet.

features.title: Take over a session another app holds; refuse writes after a takeover
features.notes: Arthur: the "another latch or Apaki window has this session open" error needs a force takeover. A pane whose session was taken over refuses to send (TAKEN_OVER) so a stale window cannot fork the conversation. Locks are Apaki's own files, not a Claude Code surface. Phone (2026-10-12): the same Session in use card and Take over here on the phone page, or Take over from a followed desktop pane (phone-shared-view).

features.title: One self-contained package: installer that waits for close, apaki command, App Paths entry
features.notes: package-apaki.ps1 builds apaki\dist\Myrlin Apaki (the exe, the engine with latch, node, bin). install-apaki.ps1 mirrors it into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Myrlin Apaki, takes -WaitForClose and -Now (in-use files are moved aside and the next open runs the new version), and one installer runs at a time. The bundled Claude Code binary comes with the SDK package, so an SDK upgrade is a repackage.

features.title: The PC checks the phone page against the site before showing a pairing code
features.notes: The phone page is a reproducible build of apaki/ui plus apaki/web; the PC builds it, fetches every file from apaki.myrlin.io, compares, and refuses to show a code if a file differs. Any change under apaki/ui or apaki/web makes a new page version that must be published before the new Apaki installs (the Phone page ... published commits).

features.title: Light and dark themes, following Windows or set by hand
features.notes: Apaki's own palette, not Claude Code's theme setting. Custom themes (#79305) are not planned.

features.title: Pair a phone with a QR code through an end-to-end relay
features.notes: Zero-knowledge pairing: P-256 key exchange, AES-256-GCM, fresh keys per connection, matching 6-digit code, Allow on the PC; the relay forwards sealed frames. The first-party equivalents are Claude Remote Control plus the Claude phone Code tab and Codex remote from the ChatGPT phone app; Apaki differs by being end to end, accepting API-key sessions and covering many accounts.

features.title: Scanning the PC code also saves a phone key and adds the PC to the account
features.notes: ENROLL.md version 2: signed via, phone-ok, Connected lets a new phone in and notifies with Block, Private asks Allow or Block. The end to end test found and fixed a race that lost the close reason (da38c13). One enrollment test (table, Private) is timing flaky under the full parallel run.

features.title: Apaki accounts with passkeys: sign in on any phone and see your PCs
features.notes: Passkey only; the vault of PCs is encrypted with a key derived from the passkey PRF, so the relay stores public keys and ciphertext.

features.title: Connected or Private mode and per-phone access: Full, No shell, Chat only
features.notes: The PC enforces the capability whatever the phone page does: tools removed from the pane's Claude Code (disallowedTools) and refused by a PreToolUse hook that holds in every permission mode. Any new Claude Code tool that edits files or runs commands must be added to CAP_BLOCKED_TOOLS: when the tool-input list gains a tool, review it here. 2026-10-12: the access level also decides which phone ops are allowed (remote-policy.js capAllowsOp): rename, forkSession, archive and folder need Full or No shell, browserView needs Full, askSearch is open to every level; a new phone op that changes what the PC keeps belongs in SESSION_WRITE_OPS.

features.title: Native iOS app around the phone client (Secure Enclave keys, Keychain pairings)
features.notes: Capacitor shell running the bundled phone page; each pairing's device key lives in the Secure Enclave and the records in the Keychain. Build 2 is on TestFlight under team F3772W8T7L; pairing links and passkeys use the association file served by the relay site.

features.title: Android app plugins (Keystore, OkHttp, code scanner)
features.notes: Plugins written to the same API as the Swift ones; not built or run on a device (no Play Store setup).

features.title: Phone page feels like an app: list home, swipe back, bottom sheets, home screen install
features.notes: Phone only: the list is home with a large title, a conversation slides in from the right, a swipe from the left edge goes back, menus and sheets rise from the bottom and close with a swipe down, pull down to refresh, installs to the Home Screen.

features.title: Hosted relay and phone page at apaki.myrlin.io, self-hostable
features.notes: One Cloudflare Worker serves the relay and the phone page; the PC builds the page itself and compares every file before showing a pairing code. Per-address and per-room budget shares, a $3 daily guard, close codes NO_PC 4404, IP_SHARE 4504, ROOM_SHARE 4505.

features.title: Any browser: sign in with the phone passkey, nothing saved, auto sign-out after inactivity
features.notes: CLOUD.md section 2: memory only (no IndexedDB, localStorage, cookies or service worker for account data), default 30 minute inactivity sign-out (5, 15, 30, 60 or 240 configurable), 60 second warning, session token 12 hours at most. Tests must assert no account data in any storage API after sign-out. Build order step 1.

features.title: Browser sessions appear on the PC as kind browser with a 7 day expiry
features.notes: Each sign-in makes a fresh per-session phone key; Connected shows "Browser session (Chrome on Windows) connected" with Block, Private asks Allow or Block; records drop from the list after 7 days unless blocked. Build order step 2.

features.title: Desktop Cloud button: sign in once, list your machines, Connect
features.notes: Passkey prompt in Apaki's web view, account session and vault key sealed with DPAPI on the PC; Connect opens the machine in its own tab running the phone client from a page version Apaki verified (version 1). Build order step 3.

features.title: Remote machines' sessions as ordinary panes next to local ones (Cloud version 2)
features.notes: The engine holds the channel and routes a pane's ops to the remote PC. Explicitly not in version 1.

features.title: Apaki Cloud paid tier: Stripe entitlement on the hosted relay, after the terms check
features.notes: Paid: passkey account, any-browser access, the desktop Cloud button, later push. Free and self-hostable: phone pairing and everything on a self-hosted relay. Blocked on written clarity from Anthropic (no offering claude.ai login or intermediating credentials) and OpenAI (app-server auth has never been permitted for hosted services); what is sold is hosting and the account service. A server and business item that gates the desktop Cloud button and the phone account routes.

features.title: Push notifications to the phone when Claude asks or finishes (later, paid)
features.notes: Same as os-notifications-and-phone-push on the phone side; kept separate because CLOUD.md files it under the paid tier.

features.title: Detect worktrees per repo and map each session's folder to its worktree
features.notes: Built 2026-10-12. findRepo reads .git, gitdir and commondir from files, so a repository with no linked worktree costs no git process; one with linked worktrees gets the porcelain worktree list and, per worktree, lines added and removed against its base, files, ahead and behind, unpushed commits and whether it is merged. Refreshed every 30 s while a window or phone is connected, and shortly after a turn ends or a pane opens. The base is the repository's default branch, or the one a worktree Apaki made came from (kept in ~/.claude/latch/apaki-worktrees.json, never in the repository). A session maps to its worktree by its folder, in the window and on the phone alike (worktree.js wtFor: the deepest worktree wins, because the main checkout's folder contains the ones Claude Code keeps under .claude/worktrees). Not built: EnterWorktree tool uses in a transcript do not yet move a session to that worktree (no transcript with a real use was found to check the format against). Codex threads are build order step 5.

features.title: Create and remove worktrees from the engine, guarded
features.notes: Built 2026-10-12. Engine ops worktreePlan and worktreeRun, kinds create, remove, commit, push, pr and merge: the plan shows the exact commands that will run (made from the same argument lists), warnings and blockers, and the engine plans again when it runs, so a client never decides what is safe. Location follows Claude Code's .claude/worktrees when the repository has one, else <repo>.worktrees/<branch>. Remove refuses the main checkout and any dirty, locked, unpushed or in-use worktree, never forces, and deletes a branch only with the safe delete once it is merged. Phone: allowed with Full access only, for folders the PC already lists; No shell and Chat only see the actions dimmed with the reason (remote-policy.js worktreePlan and worktreeRun).

features.title: New worktree option in the Starts in sheet when starting a conversation
features.notes: Built 2026-10-12. The Starts in sheet opens on This folder or New worktree; New worktree picks a repository and a base branch (default the repository's), the pane then starts in a worktree it makes on its first message: the branch is suggested from that message (editable), the command is shown, and Create it and send makes it. Phone: the same sheet. A phone cannot browse the PC's disks (the places and listDir ops are not in PHONE_OPS), so This folder lists the folders the PC already knows, which also makes the Starts in button work on the phone for the first time.

features.title: Repo-aware sidebar: worktrees under repos, branch and change count, Worktrees filter
features.notes: Built 2026-10-12. A Worktrees filter joins All and In terminals: repositories with linked worktrees, the main checkout first, then the worktree with the newest conversation, conversations nested under their worktree (six, then Show more). A row shows the branch name and the change count; colour only for conflicts, a branch behind its base and a folder that is gone; hover shows New conversation here and the menu (always shown on the phone). A conversation in a linked worktree names its branch in the All view. Same code on the phone's list, with touch sizes.

features.title: Pane branch label with View changes, Commit, Push, Open PR, Merge, Open folder, Remove
features.notes: Built 2026-10-12. The folder line gains a branch label ("fix-checkout +42 -7", a worktree glyph when it is not the main checkout) whose menu has View changes, New conversation here, Commit, Push, Open pull request (gh), Merge into the base, New worktree, Open folder, Open terminal and Remove worktree (refused with the reason shown). Every git action opens one sheet that shows the commands first. Phone: the nav row shows the same label and a tap opens the same menu. Below Full access the git actions are listed but dimmed with the reason. Open folder and Open terminal are desktop only: they open a window on the PC (the phone's session menu hides Show folder for the same reason).

features.title: Diff viewer pane (View changes) for a worktree or session
features.notes: Built 2026-10-12. A viewer pane (View changes): per file patches of everything since the branch left its base plus uncommitted work and new files, or only what is not committed, with a Commit button; saved and restored with the tab, read again when the engine reports different numbers for the folder. Big files are cut and say so. Reads through worktreeDiff, which is read only and open at every phone access level. Opens as a page in the phone's pager like any viewer. Also the consolidated review pane the market research ranks P1 (Claude VS Code #33932 204 thumbs-up, Codex #2998 235).

features.title: Tab tooltip shows a shared worktree branch; New tab in a new worktree
features.notes: Built 2026-10-12. A tab whose conversations all work in one worktree names its branch in its tooltip; a right-click on the + adds New tab in a new worktree. Desktop tab bar only: the phone has no hover and no + button, and starts a conversation in a new worktree from its Starts in sheet instead (worktree-new-on-start).

features.title: Offer removal of merged worktrees in one prompt
features.notes: Built 2026-10-12. A row at the top of the Worktrees view, "N merged worktrees can go", opens one sheet listing them; each removal is planned again by the engine (so a worktree that gained work since is kept) and the merged branch goes with it. Offered only when a branch is inside the base, had work of its own, and the worktree is clean and unlocked. Same on the phone.

features.title: Worktrees for Codex threads the same way
features.notes: Build order step 5; needs the Codex pane work first (cwd of a thread maps to a worktree like a Claude session).

features.title: Phone shows the same repo and worktree grouping, branch label, diff viewer and New worktree
features.notes: Arthur 2026-10-11: "make sure we're updating the app alongside the desktop app so all functionality is equal across the board". Built 2026-10-12 for steps 1 to 4. The window and the phone page run the same app.js, pane.js and worktree.js; the phone adds its nav-row label and touch sizes. Policy (remote-policy.js): PHONE_OPS gains worktrees and worktreeDiff (read only, every access level) and worktreePlan and worktreeRun (Full access only, create names its repository and never a place to put it, every folder must be one the PC already lists, every field is bounded); worktreeTerminal is not a phone op. The worktrees event is a broadcast, cached for phones that connect later. Desktop only by nature: Open folder, Open terminal, the + menu and the tab tooltip.

features.title: Run codex app-server as a per-engine process and speak its JSON-RPC
features.notes: One codex app-server process per engine, started the first time a Codex pane, the model list or the Codex view needs it, stopped after three minutes with no Codex pane. Per process -c overrides only (the tool server and the shell variables); ~/.codex/config.toml is never written (test: no config/*Write request). The native build is found without a shell (npm layout, PATH, APAKI_CODEX_BIN). The phone has nothing to run: its engine is the PC. Live check: APAKI_LIVE_CODEX=1 npm test reads the real server (models, config, threads, a history page) and sees the -c override as config. Not done: a separate process per Glass account.

features.title: Codex sessions indexed and searchable; a hit opens as a Codex pane
features.notes: latch-index still indexes ~/.codex/sessions as codex:<uuid>. Since 2026-10-12 a hit opens as a working Codex pane (it was read-only before); the rail row says codex, and a Codex view lists the threads.

features.title: Every Codex thread on the PC: thread/list plus rollout files the server does not list
features.notes: thread/list (cli, vscode, exec, appServer and unknown sources; recency order; the state database first, a rollout scan on refresh), shaped as session rows, plus the rollout files in ~/.codex/sessions and ~/.codex/archived_sessions (or $CODEX_HOME) for ids the server did not list (apaki/engine/codex-rollouts.js: read only, the head of each new or changed file, kept by size and time, 250 files read per refresh). Archived ones list under Archived and cannot be unarchived from Apaki. The Codex view still lists them when the server will not start. The search index now reads archived_sessions too (index/src/main.rs; a Rust change that was not built here).

features.title: Codex tab in the sidebar: search, times, archive, rename, sections both ways
features.notes: A Codex view next to All and In terminals (op codexThreads), threads out of All, search finds them (words and meaning, archived threads too), rename through thread/name/set (the Codex app shows the same name), archive in Apaki's own list (a thread archived in the Codex app lists under Archived and says so), right-click: fork (thread/fork), copy the codex resume command, folders; the same menu as a sheet on the phone. Not done: folders mapped to the Codex app's thread sections (threadSection/*, thread/section/move), which live in the Codex app's own state; times come from the server's recency time (a rollout row from the file's last write).

features.title: Codex threads open as panes in any tab next to Claude panes
features.notes: A Codex thread (codex:<id>) or a new conversation (Claude Code or Codex in the empty pane) opens in any tab, split or folder, next to Claude panes, with the same drag and drop, badge and unread; a small CODEX mark in the pane header (and the phone's nav line). The pane is the same Pane class with kind codex; a restored workspace keeps the kind; a window that comes back attaches to a running turn (open becomes attach, as for Claude). A new Claude pane never inherits a Codex pane's picks.

features.title: Codex model picker, effort picker and the approval and sandbox presets
features.notes: Model picker from model/list with each model's own efforts (the effort grid spreads them over its five columns); the Codex app's three presets in the mode chip: read-only, auto and full access (danger-full-access with approvals never, the bypass session), Shift+Tab cycles. A new thread starts with the user's own Codex config (config/read); only what was picked in the pane travels (thread/start, thread/resume and every turn/start), so a thread the Codex app made keeps its own settings until a pick. A restricted phone is read-only and never asks. Not used: thread/settings/update and turn/settings/update (the per-turn overrides carry the same).

features.title: Codex send, stop, steer (Ctrl+Enter) and queue with Edit
features.notes: Send (turn/start), Stop (turn/interrupt, the turn ends as stopped), steer (turn/steer, Ctrl+Enter or the Steer button; a steer with no turn running comes back as steer_missed and goes out as a message), the queue with Edit, Up arrow to edit, the engine sending the queue when no window is connected: all the same code as for Claude, worded for Codex (checked in the demo window: Enter queues, the Queued card has Steer, Edit and a remove button). The server side queue (thread/queue/*, thread/queue/changed) is experimental and is not used: Apaki's own queue does the same job for both agents, and the server's only matters for a thread another client also drives.

features.title: Attach images and files, paste, drag in; voice into the box
features.notes: Pictures go inline (image items as data URLs); other files (paste, drop, the attach button; up to 6 MB, four per message from a phone) are saved under the latch folder's codex-attachments/<thread> with a _WHY_THIS_IS_HERE.md and mentioned by path. Voice is the pane's own Whisper path (the mic button), unchanged. The phone has no voice (the phone keyboard dictates), as for Claude. Not used: thread/attachment/*.

features.title: Slash commands Codex offers, plus Apaki's own
features.notes: In the pane: /new, /resume, /model, /effort, /approvals, /folder, /fork; from the engine: /compact, /status, /review (uncommitted changes, branch <name>, commit <sha>, or free instructions), /diff, /mcp, /goal, /revert, /init (a turn that asks for an AGENTS.md), /mention <file> (attached to the next message as a mention item, once). The server has no command list, so Codex's own list is its skills (skills/list): the enabled ones follow the commands in the slash menu (never shadowing a command) and /name words sends one as $name in the text plus a skill input item, as the Codex app does. Phones type the same words; /revert and a goal change are refused to a Chat only phone.

features.title: Codex context meter, compaction and auto-compact settings
features.notes: The meter is the last call's tokens over the model's context window (thread/tokenUsage/updated), with the split (input, cached, output, reasoning); it shows once a turn has run (a resumed thread has no usage until then). Its tooltip says where Codex compacts on its own when the user's model_auto_compact_token_limit is set. Compact now (the meter's menu or /compact) runs thread/compact/start and the compaction shows as a divider. Not done: changing the auto-compact setting (a Codex config key; Apaki never writes ~/.codex/config.toml).

features.title: Streaming Codex agent messages and reasoning summaries like Claude's thinking
features.notes: Agent messages stream as the SDK's text deltas, so the pane draws them as it draws Claude's; the reasoning summary is a collapsed Thinking line (the working line takes a thinking word while it runs); turn/start asks for summary auto.

features.title: Codex plans shown as a checklist
features.notes: turn/plan/updated is a TodoWrite call (inProgress is in_progress), so Codex's plan is the same checklist card, updated in place. A proposed plan item (Plan mode text) is shown as the assistant's text. Not done: the Plan collaboration mode toggle.

features.title: Codex command runs with live output
features.notes: A command is a Bash (or PowerShell) line with the shell wrapper taken off; its output streams into the line while it runs (150 ms, the newest 40,000 characters), and the result replaces it with the exit code on failure.

features.title: Codex file changes with diffs, openable in a viewer
features.notes: A file change is a Patch line with a header per file and its hunks in red and green; the turn's whole diff becomes a card (via codex-diff, no viewer pops up by itself) that opens in the viewer; /diff shows the last turn's again. patchUpdated (streaming patches) is not drawn live.

features.title: Codex MCP tool calls, web searches, images and sub-agent items
features.notes: MCP tool calls read like Claude's (mcp__server__tool, with image results), web searches list their results, pictures Codex looked at or made become a card, sub-agent items are tool lines. Not done: opening a sub-agent's own thread as a viewer.

features.title: Codex errors, retries and model reroutes
features.notes: A failed turn is a failed result with the server's reason in words (usage limit, context window, sign-in); a retry is a system line; a reroute says from which model to which and why; a server that dies ends the running turns with a message and the next message resumes the thread.

features.title: Codex hooks as system lines like Claude's
features.notes: A failed, blocked or stopped hook (or a quiet success with a warning) is a system line through notices.js, as Claude Code prints its own; a quiet success is not shown.

features.title: Codex full history from the rollout, paged like Claude's
features.notes: History pages by thread/turns/list (newest first, eight turns a request, itemsView full; rollouts reach 1.3 GB so thread/read with turns is never used). Load earlier, scroll near the top and Load all work as for Claude; the loader says how many messages are loaded (the server gives no total). The drift check compares the thread's updatedAt.

features.title: Your prompts: an exact "N of M" pin and a list of every prompt, Claude and Codex
features.notes: 2026-10-12, Arthur: the prompt list "is 100% accurate". One rule (history.js promptOf) marks every user message as a prompt or not; the pane draws a bubble for exactly those and pages count exactly those (system reminders, task notifications, local commands, hook output, bash mode and interruptions are not prompts; skill commands are, as /name args). A Codex page counts the prompts before it from the turn summaries (itemsView summary); steered messages count once their turn loads, and the pin says M+ until the count arrives. N of M opens the list of every prompt (op historyPrompts); picking one that is not loaded loads back to it in one page (historyBefore until). Pages load ahead of the reader, 1.5 screens from the top. Checked in a real browser on a 600 prompt synthetic conversation; the phone shares pane.js and the op is allowed by remote-policy.js.

features.title: Codex threads: last message times in the list, one row per thread in search
features.notes: 2026-10-12 parity audit (CODEX.md). A row's time is its last message, read from the rollout's tail (recencyAt is when the last turn started; the file's time moves with token counts). A search or Ask Claude hit on a Codex thread shows the Codex view's row (its name and time) instead of a separate "Codex: first prompt" row; the no-index quick filter matches Codex threads too.

features.title: Codex question card in the pane (request_user_input), same as Claude's AskUserQuestion
features.notes: The same sheet as Claude's AskUserQuestion (options, a typed answer), headed by whose question it is; isSecret questions hide what is typed; answered once; a skip answers nothing; serverRequest/resolved drops a stale sheet. Multi-select does not exist in Codex's questions. 2026-10-12, later (Arthur: "it should be shown in the pane and not lock the user from using the app"): no longer a sheet over the window. It is a card in the pane that asked, docked above its message box (apaki/ui/askcard.js), numbered rows like Claude Code's terminal; the rest of the window stays usable, several panes can wait at once, numbers and Enter answer only the focused pane's card, Esc goes back to the message box without answering, the tab and the header say Waiting for you and the taskbar badge counts it; ask_gone carries why and by, so a card settled elsewhere leaves one line (Answered on a phone, the turn ended).

features.title: Codex approvals: command, file change, permissions and the older exec and patch approvals
features.notes: Command, file change, permissions and the older exec and patch approvals use the permission sheet with Codex's words (Approve once, Approve for this session, Deny) and the command or the diff shown; an unreadable answer declines; Deny with a note sends the note to the model as a steer. A request nobody can answer (a thread with no pane) is declined at once. Not done: acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment (offered as the session approval where the server lists no session decision). 2026-10-12, later (Arthur: "it should be shown in the pane and not lock the user from using the app"): no longer a sheet over the window. It is a card in the pane that asked, docked above its message box (apaki/ui/askcard.js), numbered rows like Claude Code's terminal; the rest of the window stays usable, several panes can wait at once, numbers and Enter answer only the focused pane's card, Esc goes back to the message box without answering, the tab and the header say Waiting for you and the taskbar badge counts it; ask_gone carries why and by, so a card settled elsewhere leaves one line (Answered on a phone, the turn ended).

features.title: Codex MCP elicitation: a form from the tool server's schema
features.notes: A tool-call approval (Codex marks it in _meta) is a permission sheet, a form is the question sheet (one question per field; enums, yes or no and text), a link asks first and then opens in Apaki's browser. The shapes were written from the schema and run end to end against the fake app-server; none was seen live (no turn was started on a real account). The openai/form variants and user verification are declined, never left waiting. 2026-10-12, later (Arthur: "it should be shown in the pane and not lock the user from using the app"): no longer a sheet over the window. It is a card in the pane that asked, docked above its message box (apaki/ui/askcard.js), numbered rows like Claude Code's terminal; the rest of the window stays usable, several panes can wait at once, numbers and Enter answer only the focused pane's card, Esc goes back to the message box without answering, the tab and the header say Waiting for you and the taskbar badge counts it; ask_gone carries why and by, so a card settled elsewhere leaves one line (Answered on a phone, the turn ended).

features.title: Claude Code MCP elicitation and user dialogs
features.notes: Not built and not requested. Without onElicitation an MCP server that asks the user for input is declined by the SDK. Recorded as the Claude side of codex-mcp-elicitation so the two stay together.

features.title: Codex questions and approvals from a phone through the phone policy
features.notes: The phone page shares apaki/ui, so the sheets are the same. The policy allows codex: session ids, Codex's model ids, efforts and presets on Codex panes (and Claude's on Claude panes), files, and the two read only ops codexModels and codexThreads; a restricted phone gets read-only and never prompts, and Apaki's tools are refused for it.

features.title: Apaki's show and browser tools offered to Codex (per process MCP server)
features.notes: Done as the per process MCP server the contract allows, not as dynamic tools: dynamic tools exist only on thread/start, so a resumed thread (the common case) would have none. The process gets -c mcp_servers.apaki.* (command, args, env; startup 30 s, tool 120 s); the stdio server lists show and the six browser tools and forwards each call to the engine (POST /tool, the process's token), which runs it for the pane whose turn is running (a thread id in the call's _meta wins, if the server ever sends one). item/tool/call is answered with a failure for any tool Apaki does not provide. Not verified live: no turn was started on a real account, so whether the model calls the tools was seen only in the fake-server tests.

features.title: Per-thread developer instructions saying the Apaki tools exist
features.notes: One paragraph (DEV_INSTRUCTIONS) sent as developerInstructions on thread/start and thread/resume, so a thread the Codex app made learns it when opened here: the tools exist, use show instead of start, explorer or xdg-open, inline what is shown, use the browser tools to check web work.

features.title: BROWSER pointed at Apaki's shim in the app-server environment
features.notes: BROWSER, APAKI_OPEN_URL, the token and APAKI_NODE are set for the process and, through shell_environment_policy.set (the default policy drops names holding TOKEN), for the commands Codex runs; a link they open reaches the engine's /open and lands in the browser pane of the pane whose turn runs. Windows only, like Claude's (the shim is a .cmd).

features.title: Match the Codex app's side panel: diffs, files, images, terminal output, web pages
features.notes: Diffs (the turn's changes as a card that opens in the viewer), images (shown as the Codex app shows them), command output (live in the tool line, then the final result) and web pages (the browser pane) are shown. A changed file's name in a patch header now opens that file in the viewer (op codexOpenFile; only files this conversation changed, also those read from its history; a phone may ask the same through the policy). Not done: a preview of a file Codex only read, and a terminal view of a running command in its own pane.

features.title: Myrlin Glass for Codex: signed-in account, rate limits, swaps reflected live
features.notes: The pane's billing chip shows the signed-in account (account/read: ChatGPT and the plan, or API key) and follows account/updated; its tooltip lists the plan windows (account/rateLimits/read, kept current by account/rateLimits/updated) and the worst one shows beside the account name; at 80 percent and above the same usage warning Claude shows (five hour, weekly). Swaps stay Glass's: the corner card still switches the live login. Not verified: whether a Glass swap while the app-server runs sends account/updated.

features.title: Codex review mode, revert and fork
features.notes: /review (review/start) takes the uncommitted changes, a base branch, a commit or free instructions; fork from the right-click menu and /fork (thread/fork); /revert takes the newest turn out of the thread (thread/revert, then the pane is drawn again from the server) and leaves the files Codex changed alone. Tested against the fake app-server; the semantics of thread/revert were read from the schema only (a real thread was not changed).

features.title: Codex goals
features.notes: /goal sets (thread/goal/set, origin user), shows (thread/goal/get) and clears (thread/goal/clear) the thread's goal; when Codex moves it (done, blocked, out of budget, or changed in the Codex app) a line says so, once per change of state (thread/goal/updated and cleared). Not shown: a standing goal indicator in the pane header. Claude Code's own goal concept (active_goal, ProposeGoal) is still not shown.

features.title: Phone access: Codex panes on the phone with the same caps
features.notes: Codex panes on the phone with the same caps (read-only for No shell and Chat only, enforced in the engine). The phone's nav line says Codex. Looked at in the demo harness (phone.html?ws=codex); not run against a real relay and phone.

features.title: Never touch or close the ChatGPT or Codex desktop apps; read only
features.notes: Apaki starts and stops only its own app-server process (by its own handle); the Codex and ChatGPT desktop apps are never touched. What it reads of ~/.codex is through that server's thread/list, thread/turns/list, model/list and config/read.

features.title: Start a new Codex conversation from the empty pane
features.notes: The empty pane offers Claude Code or Codex; Codex starts a thread with the first message (thread/start with the folder, any picked model and preset, and the developer instructions), so no thread exists until something is sent. Phone and desktop alike.

features.title: Session list like the ChatGPT app: one line per session, recency groups, exact times, a hover card
features.notes: Arthur 2026-10-12: "think about chatgpt app and how the sessions are displayed". A row is the name, cut, and the last message's time in a short form (now, 12m, the clock today, a weekday and the time this week, then the date), under Pinned, Today, Yesterday, Previous 7 days, Previous 30 days, then each month. Then Myrlin Glass's list design (Arthur: "myrlin glass ui/ux is much clearer, we want to borrow from it"): one leading glyph per row carries the provider and the state (Claude's spark in Claude orange, Codex's hexagon in Codex green, a turning arc when working, an amber bubble when it waits for your answer, a terminal, an archived copy), the name in a strong weight, the time right-aligned in a muted mono, hover and selection a soft fill with no borders, hairlines only between groups; never a pill. The row in the focused pane or under the keyboard eases open a second line (folder, branch, model, size, subagents). Hover (setTip): the full name, the exact date and time, folder, branch or worktree, agent, model, size, state. Keys: arrows, Home, End, Enter, F2, Alt+Enter, the context menu key. Phone: the same rows 48 px tall, no hover (the long press menu instead). Evaluated in the demo harness at 1440x900, the narrowest sidebar and 390x844, light and dark, reduced motion.

features.title: Folders open and close in place in the sidebar, several at once, remembered
features.notes: Arthur 2026-10-12: "the folders should expand when clicked on and contract when clicked on again instead of just transitioning the entire sidepanel". A click opens a folder's sessions under it (grid rows 0fr to 1fr, no layout property animated, off under reduced motion), a second click closes it; several can be open; the open ones are kept in localStorage and the saved workspace. Dropping a session on a folder still moves it in; Show only this folder (the old view) is in the folder's menu with Rename and Delete. Keys: Enter or Space, Right and Left, arrows, F2. Phone: a tap opens or closes, a long press opens the folder's menu (Open or Close, Show only this folder; renaming and deleting folders stay on the PC), the rows under a folder open like the list's.

features.title: Session Details: every fact about a conversation, with copy buttons
features.notes: Right click > Details (or Alt+Enter). The list's facts show at once; op sessionInfo (read only, every phone access level) adds what the transcript or rollout says: created and last message (exact, local time), prompts counted by the pane's rule (history.js promptOf), replies once per API message, tool calls, compactions, tokens, models used and the last, effort, Claude Code or Codex version, branch, the folder it last ran in, size on disk with the side folder, subagents and background shells, archive, pin, terminal and the panes holding it (model, effort, permissions, billing). Copy buttons for the id, folder, transcript and resume command; Show (Explorer) and Export on the PC only.

features.title: Session menu: Pin to top, Open beside, Open in a terminal, Export as Markdown, Ask Claude about it, Details
features.notes: Arthur 2026-10-12: "think about everything a user might want to do with a session". The menu (right click, the row's ... button, the context menu key): Open, Open beside, Open in a new tab, Open here, Open in a terminal (sends the engine op openTerminal { sessionId, kind, paneId? }, which the console toggle's work builds: the exact session in a terminal window with the pane's settings), Stop and Close its pane when they apply, Rename, Pin to top (latch/pinned.json, shared with the phone), Move to folder, Fork, Archive or Unarchive, Ask Claude about it (a new conversation in its folder with where the transcript is), Export as Markdown (Downloads, shown in Explorer), its subagents, Copy session id, Copy resume command, Show folder in Explorer, Details. Phone: Details, Pin (Full and No shell), Ask Claude, Export (the Markdown comes back as text and is saved on the phone); left out on purpose, so the phone stays partial: Open in a terminal and Show folder in Explorer, which open windows on the PC.

features.title: Codex threads in the main session list from startup, beside Claude's, without starting the app-server
features.notes: Arthur 2026-10-12: Codex sessions integrated exactly like Claude's. The engine reads the rollout files (read only) without the app-server, times each by its last message and keeps what it read in latch/codex-list.json, so a restart lists them at once and reads only new or changed rollouts; a background pass runs at most every 30 s and sends the list again only when it changed. Measured on this PC: 1,804 rollouts, a warm pass about 130 ms. The Codex view's rows (names set in Codex) win for the same thread. In the window they sit in All with Claude's under the same recency headings, with a small Codex mark, the same hover card, menu and Details; Archive works on them (archive.js takes codex: ids).
